Information is understood and compared easily when graphs are used because they illustrate the facts and numbers.
For example, you can quickly tell when the Dow Jones Stock Index is increasing or decreasing by looking at the graph.
DOW JONES STOCK INDEX
Using the actual numbers does not show the trend. You would have to study the value of the Index for each day for the entire year.
The graph illustrates all the numbers so they can be analyzed quickly.

DISCUSSION
The rectangular coordinate system is made by joining a horizontal and a vertical number line.
The rectangular coordinate system is made by joining a horizontal and a vertical number line.
NUMBER LINE - A number line is a graphic representation of a series of numbers. Each number is associated with a point on the line.
The horizontal line is called the X-axis.
The X-axis and Y-axis intersect at the zero point of each line. The point of intersection is called the origin.

The grid formed by the X-axis and Y-axis is used to graph equations and to identify any point on the graph.
A point on a graph is identified by a pair of numbers called an ordered pair or coordinates.
The first number of the ordered pair is called the abscissa or
The X-coordinate measures the horizontal distance of the point from the origin. This number relates to a value from the X-axis.
This point is three horizontal units from the origin.
The second number of the ordered pair is called the ordinate or Y-coordinate.
The Y-coordinate measures the vertical distance of the point from the origin. This number relates to a value from the Y-axis.
This point is 4 vertical units from the origin.
The coordinates of a point describe the horizontal and vertical placement of that point.
The order in which the coordinates are written is important.
The point (3,4) is not the same as the point (4,3)

You can tell how steep a hill is by looking at it from the side.
The slope of the hill on the right is obviously greater than the one on the left.
Graphs are linear equations also have specific angles or slopes.
Finding the slope of a line is easy when the equation is written in the slope-intercept form.
The "m" is the coefficient of X and is also the slope of the line.
The slope of a whole number is steeper than the slope of a fraction.
The "b'' is the Y-coordinate of the point where the line crosses the Y-axis, also called the Y-intercept.
This example shows how a negative slope slants toward the upper left corner while a positive slants to the upper right corner.
Always change the equation into the Y = mX + b form in order to find the slope.
The slope of a line can also be found by using the coordinates from two points with the Slope Formula.
The formula is easy to remember since the slope of a line is the rise (change in Y value) over the run (change in X value).
Place the X-coordinate and Y-coordinate from the second point into the formula.
